# Claims

1. A system comprising:
   one or more processors; and
   one or more non-transitory computer-readable media storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the system to:
   receive sensor data from a plurality of sensors;
   for each sensor of the plurality of sensors, compare a reading of the sensor with a first threshold and a second threshold;
   select, from the group consisting of a warning mode, a standby mode, and an active mode, an operating mode based on the comparison; and
   store the operating mode in a memory.

2. The system of claim 1, wherein each of the sensors comprises a temperature sensor.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein the first threshold is greater than the second threshold.

4. The system of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the system to transmit the operating mode to at least one remote device, and wherein the at least one remote device is a mobile phone.

5. A helmet comprising:
   a shell having an outer surface and an inner surface;
   a first end and a second end opposite the first end;
   at least one light mounted on the outer surface of the shell adjacent to the second end; and
   a strap coupled to the shell, the strap having a buckle.

6. The helmet of claim 5, wherein the at least one light comprises first and second light-emitting diodes, and the first and second light-emitting diodes are spaced apart along the outer surface.

7. The helmet of claim 5, wherein the strap extends between the first end and the second end, and the buckle is releasably attached to the strap.

8. The helmet of claim 5, wherein the shell is made of polycarbonate and the inner surface is lined with foam.

9. The helmet of claim 5, wherein a thickness of the shell at the first end is the same as the thickness of the shell at the second end.

10. The helmet of claim 5, further comprising a battery housing attached to the inner surface, wherein the battery housing holds a rechargeable battery that powers the at least one light.

11. The helmet of claim 10, wherein the rechargeable battery is removable from the battery housing.

12. A method comprising:
    capturing, with a camera, a plurality of images of a scene;
    generating, by a processor, a depth map from the images;
    identifying an object in the scene based on the depth map; and
    displaying, on a display, an indication of the object.

13. The method of claim 12, wherein the images are captured at a frame rate of at least 30 frames per second.

14. The method of claim 12, wherein generating the depth map comprises computing a disparity between a first image of the images and a second image of the images.

15. The method of claim 14, wherein the indication is overlaid on one of the images, and the processor determines a distance to the object from the disparity.

16. The method of claim 12, further comprising receiving, from a user, a selection of the object, wherein the processor tracks the selected object in subsequent images.
